persistency_population.note: Persistency covers only Premium paying (regular) and Lapsed policies; Surrendered and Death policies are absent by design.

data_quality_findings.finding: One AppID is stored in Excel scientific notation '1.50E+10' in Owner_Details and Persistency_Details. It is the only 8-character AppID in either file; every other AppID is 11 characters.
data_quality_findings.impact: Breaks the Policy-Owner and Policy-Persistency join for exactly one policy.
data_quality_findings.handling: NOT silently repaired. The loader exposes it as an explicit, logged repair rule (config: repair_scientific_notation_appid). When disabled, the row is reported as an orphan rather than guessed.

data_quality_findings.finding: Both Policy date columns mix separators ('/' and '-') within the same column. All values are month-first; the dash-separated subset is ambiguous on its own and was resolved by cross-validation.
data_quality_findings.impact: Naive single-format parsing silently drops ~17-33% of rows.
data_quality_findings.handling: Contract prescribes the ordered format list ['%m/%d/%Y', '%m-%d-%Y'].

data_quality_findings.finding: Monetary values are stored as text with thousands separators, including Indian lakh grouping (e.g. '12,50,000.00', '1,66,500').
data_quality_findings.impact: float() on the raw string raises; naive coercion yields nulls.
data_quality_findings.handling: Contract prescribes comma stripping before numeric coercion.

data_quality_findings.finding: Claim date columns are predominantly '%d-%b-%y' but contain a small number of '%m/%d/%Y' values. The single unsettled claim carries the literal string 'WIP' in three columns at once - Status.of.Claim, Amount.Paid and Settlement.Date - so 'WIP' is a sentinel in a monetary and a date column, not only in the status column.
data_quality_findings.impact: Settlement-lag and amount-paid metrics must exclude the unsettled claim rather than coerce 'WIP' to zero or null silently.
data_quality_findings.handling: 'WIP' is a declared sentinel meaning not-yet-settled. It is treated as missing for date and money maths, and the claim is excluded from settlement-lag and payout-ratio metrics with the exclusion reported.

data_quality_findings.finding: First Year Persistency Rate is null for a material share of agents.
data_quality_findings.impact: Agent persistency rankings must declare the eligible population.
data_quality_findings.handling: Rankings exclude null-rate agents and report the excluded count.

data_quality_findings.finding: Persistency_Details contains only Premium paying (regular) and Lapsed policies. Surrendered and Death policies have no persistency row.

evidence.note: Persistency covers only Premium paying (regular) and Lapsed policies; Surrendered and Death policies are absent by design.

data_quality_findings.impact: Persistency metrics computed over Policy_Details would use a wrong denominator.
data_quality_findings.handling: Persistency PSs declare the eligible population explicitly.

data_quality_findings.finding: Claims and Persistency are 1:1 with Policy in this dataset, not 1:N as the documented relationship allows. At most one claim row exists per policy.
data_quality_findings.impact: Joins cannot fan out, but code must not hard-code the 1:1 assumption.
data_quality_findings.handling: Joins remain many-safe; row-count assertions guard against silent fan-out.

data_quality_findings.finding: CHANNEL is 'Banca' for all 25,000 rows and Mode is 'Annually' for all rows.
data_quality_findings.impact: Channel and payment-mode comparison questions cannot be answered.
data_quality_findings.handling: No PS may offer channel or mode comparison; the limitation is stated.

data_quality_findings.finding: Owner attributes contain implausible values: ages as low as 1, an earned income up to 8,384,891,049, postal codes as low as 1, and a third gender code 'C' alongside M/F.
data_quality_findings.impact: Means are distorted by extreme values; demographic PSs need medians or caveats.
data_quality_findings.handling: Distribution PSs report medians alongside means and flag outliers.

data_quality_findings.finding: Inforce.month is an unpadded YYYYM/YYYYMM integer: '20231' means 2023-01 while '202310' means 2023-10. Lexical or numeric sorting is wrong.
data_quality_findings.impact: Trend ordering breaks unless the field is decomposed into year and month.
data_quality_findings.handling: Contract prescribes deriving period from Inforce.Date, not this column.

data_quality_findings.finding: A policy has a Login.Date later than its Inforce.Date.
data_quality_findings.impact: Underwriting-turnaround metrics can produce a negative duration.
data_quality_findings.handling: Turnaround PSs report and exclude negative durations.

data_quality_findings.finding: Owner.Comm.Postal.Code is not numeric. Two records hold alphanumeric foreign postal codes, matching owners with a non-India address.
data_quality_findings.impact: Coercing the column to a number silently discards these two values and would strip leading zeros from any code that has one.
data_quality_findings.handling: The column is typed as an identifier and kept as text. Identifier columns are never summed or averaged, and join keys compare exactly rather than through floating-point equality.

data_quality_findings.finding: Twelve columns are numeric-looking identifiers or codes rather than quantities: AppID, ClientID, SALES_ID, Branch_No, Claim_No, Inforce.month and Owner.Comm.Postal.Code.
data_quality_findings.impact: Typed as numbers they would permit meaningless arithmetic such as an average AppID, and would make every join depend on float equality.
data_quality_findings.handling: All are typed as identifiers and held as text throughout the system.

Policy.Mode has a single value ('Annually'). Persistency.Payment_Mode does vary.
